source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED requires a vendor session selector/handle, privilege schema and rollback because it interprets the command as a possibly persistent privilege write against an arbitrary session or account.

old_problem: The historical review correctly recognized the authorization risk but assigned the wrong target semantics: standard Set Session Privilege Level does not accept a session handle, user ID or channel selector and does not persistently rewrite account/channel policy. It is authenticated App command 3Bh sent by the active session to change only that session's present privilege, bounded by the already negotiated session maximum plus user and channel limits. Requiring an unknown vendor method therefore left a standard command falsely blocked.
disposition_reason: Replace the vendor-dependent interpretation with the official App 06h/3Bh contract. In one isolated authenticated test session whose negotiated, user and channel ceilings are exactly Operator, first query current privilege with request 00h and require initial User 02h, change that same session to Operator with 03h, query it again, restore it to User with 02h, query once more, and close only that session. The response byte is the authoritative present/new privilege. Administrator/OEM, reserved values, account/channel writes, unrelated sessions, automatic retry and generic log clearing are excluded. Runtime target, test identity, limit evidence, persistent-session harness and security approval are finite Project inputs rather than missing command semantics.
decision_basis: Master XLSX row 1017, physical adjacent row 1018, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The code occurs only once. Formal queue sequence 60 was independently verified as row 1021 / variant 1df38d1667d906be.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.18 says this command is sent in authenticated format and acts on the session carrying it. A non-Callback session begins at User even when a higher maximum was negotiated; the console uses this command to raise the present session level.

Table 22-24 defines a single request byte: 00h returns the present level without changing it, 02h selects User, 03h Operator, 04h Administrator and 05h OEM; 01h and all other values are reserved. Success returns one byte containing the new or present privilege.

The requested level cannot exceed the session's negotiated maximum or the effective lower user/channel limit. Command-specific failures are 80h requested level unavailable, 81h above channel/user limit and 82h unable to disable User-level authentication; none may be treated as PASS or retried automatically.

Because no handle, User ID or channel appears in the request, this row must not be implemented with Set User Access or Set Channel Access and must not claim persistent role mutation. Those are separate source identities later in the workbook.

A stock `ipmitool raw` invocation normally establishes and tears down its own connection and may automatically elevate it according to `-L`; multiple independent invocations therefore cannot prove ordered state transitions within one session. A validated persistent-session transport with packet/response evidence is required.

ED-03/ED-13 allow a standard IPMI contract while prohibiting OEM guesses; ED-18/ED-30 require explicit authorization boundaries; ED-19 preserves security evidence; ED-28 requires isolation and recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 govern package readiness, user confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict separation.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set Session Privilege Level (App 06h/3Bh) current-session transition and restoration
test_case.purpose: Prove that one dedicated authenticated session reports its initial User privilege, can change only its own present privilege to the approved Operator ceiling, reports that state accurately, returns to User, and closes without changing any account, channel or unrelated session.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware and session-based management channel supporting standard App 06h/3Bh, with exact channel number and capability evidence
Dedicated ephemeral test identity whose per-user limit, channel limit and negotiated session maximum are all explicitly approved at Operator (03h), plus an independent Administrator recovery observer

Validated persistent-session IPMI transport/harness that exposes the authenticated 3Bh request, completion code and response byte for several commands on the same Session ID; package version/hash and secret-safe logging configuration

Pre/post Get User Access and Get Channel Access read-only baselines proving that the test must not persistently alter those limits, plus active-session inventory/correlation and supported exact Close Session cleanup

Security point confirmation binding target, account, channel, maximum privilege, request sequence 00h/03h/00h/02h/00h, redaction, observer and recovery; no production identity or generic Administrator/OEM request
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SECURITY-CONFORMANCE PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve audit logs and read-only user/channel/session baselines; do not clear logs. Establish exactly one dedicated authenticated session with negotiated maximum Operator, while retaining its initial User level and a positively correlated Session ID. The same persistent session must send these App NetFn 06h / command 3Bh requests in order with no reconnect: (1) data 00h; require completion 00h and response byte 02h, (2) data 03h; require 00h/03h, (3) data 00h; require 00h/03h, (4) data 02h; require 00h/02h, (5) data 00h; require 00h/02h. Capture authenticated packet structure, monotonic session sequence and redacted correlation without credentials or reusable Session IDs. Send no command requiring Operator privilege merely to demonstrate authority. Close only the correlated test session, prove it disappeared, and repeat read-only user/channel baselines to show no persistent policy change. Never use separate raw invocations as one state machine, request Administrator/OEM, send reserved values, modify user/channel access, clear logs, touch unrelated sessions or retry a timeout/failure.
test_case.expected_result: All five exchanges occur on one authenticated correlated session. The initial no-change query returns User 02h; the approved 03h request and following query both return Operator 03h; restoration 02h and its query both return User 02h. Every exchange has completion 00h, reserved bits are zero and authenticated session sequences remain valid. The exact session then closes, all preexisting sessions and management access remain healthy, user/channel limits and audit records are unchanged, and no secret or reusable raw identifier is retained. Any 80h-82h or generic failure, wrong level, reconnect, unintended persistent mutation, ambiguous timeout or failed cleanup is FAIL/NOT READY without retry.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires source identity, one approved persistent authenticated session, initial User state, exact 00h→02h / 03h→03h / 00h→03h / 02h→02h / 00h→02h response sequence, valid per-message/session sequencing, precise close and unchanged account/channel/unrelated-session/audit baselines. A high-level login alone, multiple independently created sessions, only a successful Operator command, response without completion/Session-ID correlation, Administrator/OEM or reserved request, 80h/81h/82h, automatic privilege elevation hidden by the tool, account/channel policy write, log clearing, secret disclosure, retry, access loss or incomplete restoration cannot pass. Missing approved limits, harness or observer is NOT READY rather than Pending review.
safety_gate: Use an isolated management network, dedicated disposable identity and least ceiling sufficient for this coverage: Operator only. Production/admin identities and Administrator/OEM transitions are out of scope.
Confirm user, channel and negotiated session limits before opening the test session. Do not change those limits to make the test pass; a mismatch is a Project configuration issue.

The tool must keep one session open and expose command-level evidence. Reject workflows where each raw command silently opens a new session or where the client already elevated before the initial 00h query.
Preserve audit/security logs and redact passwords, keys, authentication material and reusable Session IDs. Never use the source boilerplate log-clear step for this security test.
After reaching Operator send only another 3Bh query/restore and exact Close Session; do not use the temporary authority for power, configuration, user, channel, firmware or session-control actions.

No automatic retry. On timeout, wrong response, sequence/auth failure, access degradation or uncertain session identity, stop writes and let the independent security owner reconcile and close only the correlated test session.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, target BMC firmware/channel and official 3Bh command mapping
Security approval and redacted dedicated identity; read-only user/channel limits and negotiated Operator session ceiling
Harness name/version/hash and proof that all five requests share one authenticated Session ID with valid monotonic sequence
Redacted request/response ledger for 00h,03h,00h,02h,00h including completion codes and exact response bytes
Pre/post user/channel access comparison proving no persistent privilege-policy mutation
Exact-session close, unchanged preexisting sessions/management access, preserved audit records, cleanup/recovery evidence and engineer PASS/FAIL/NOT READY verdict
test_case.recovery: The normal rollback is the same-session 02h request followed by 00h verification and exact Close Session. If any response or timeout is ambiguous, do not resend 3Bh and do not guess a Session ID. Preserve redacted traces, use the independent observer plus dedicated-account/time/channel correlation to identify only the test session, close it through the approved management path, and verify user/channel limits, preexisting sessions, audit integrity and management access. If the test identity or authentication material is exposed, revoke/rotate only that identity. Persistent policy drift means the wrong command/path was used: stop, restore from the read-only baseline under the security owner, and record FAIL.

source_conflict.reason: Official section 22.18 supplies the missing procedure and acceptance contract and proves the command targets the carrying session, not a vendor-selected account/session. The source's generic log-clear boilerplate is excluded because it conflicts with required security evidence.

blocked.reason: Core command identity, request values, response values, limits and restoration are standardized. Target/channel, dedicated identity, approved Operator ceiling and persistent-session harness are finite execution prerequisites, not unresolved engineering semantics.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Target BMC/firmware/channel; dedicated test identity; user/channel/session maximum fixed at Operator; validated persistent-session harness; independent observer; audit/redaction and exact-close recovery approval.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Section 22.18/Table 22-24 defines authenticated current-session behavior, initial privilege, byte values, returned privilege and 80h-82h errors; sections 6.8 and 22.17 define channel/user/session ceilings.

external_authorities.title: ipmitool upstream manual and implementation
external_authorities.application: Confirms `-L` controls remote session privilege and that client session establishment may perform privilege negotiation automatically; used to reject independent CLI invocations as proof of one ordered session state machine.

project_authority: The Project security/BMC owners supply the isolated identity, target/channel, exact effective ceilings, approved persistent-session harness, observer and cleanup window, and issue the DUT verdict. They may mark a truly unsupported command N/A only with authoritative platform capability/SPEC evidence; they cannot substitute persistent user/channel writes, production credentials, Administrator/OEM elevation, hidden reconnects, log clearing, automatic retry or incomplete restoration.
